# Omniverse interoperability profile

Version-pinned Omniverse interoperability profile for `0.12.3-alpha`. Generated from `eng/omniverse-profile.json`; do
not edit by hand. Feature and exclusion status is always resolved live from `eng/support-manifest.json` -- this document
never fabricates a status independently of that manifest. See [`docs/support-matrix.md`](support-matrix.md) for
narrative detail and [`docs/support-manifest.md`](support-manifest.md) for the full executable summary.

## Dependency baselines

- **`openusd`** (runtime-pinned, version `26.05`)
  Pinned OpenUSD core version this runtime builds against and this profile targets for interchange.
- **`materialx`** (runtime-pinned, version `1.39.4`)
  Pinned MaterialX SDK version behind the bounded MaterialX projection; MaterialX 1.39 adds the OpenPBR node
  definitions this profile's accepted corpus targets.
- **`kit-baseline`** (external-optional, version `pending`)
  Named Omniverse Kit baseline(s) this profile targets for interchange evidence. Tracked by its own dependency id and,
  once authorized, its own repository-relative provenance source; never inferred or copied from the openusd dependency
  version.
- **`usd-exchange`** (external-optional, version `pending`)
  NVIDIA usd-exchange SDK baseline used only to validate authored-asset interchange with Kit tooling. Tracked by its
  own dependency id and, once authorized, its own repository-relative provenance source.
- **`mdl-sdk`** (external-optional, version `2026.0.2`)
  Pinned NVIDIA MDL SDK baseline for the optional SDK-backed openusd_mdl_sdk adapter. eng/fetch-mdl-sdk.ps1 acquires
  it on demand for developers and CI, verified against the SHA-256 recorded in eng/mdl.lock.json; this repository
  vendors no part of it, links nothing against it, and redistributes it in no package. The shipped-by-default path has
  no MDL adapter at all, and the dependency-free openusd_mdl adapter distils authored USD input values without opening
  a module. The baseline is BSD-3-Clause, not Apache-2.0. The base runtime never depends on this; it stays out of
  Core/Imaging/Viewer/MCP packages.
- **`physx-schema-test-only`** (external-test-only, version `pending`)
  Externally supplied PhysxSchema/plugin tree used only by opt-in integration tests against an externally supplied
  Kit/schema environment. Never vendored into shipped packages.

## Permanent proprietary exclusions

- **`omniverse-rtx`** (Unreachable)
  Closed NVIDIA platform pieces; not open standards this runtime can ship or reimplement.
- **`cesium-fabric-path`** (Unreachable)
  Bypasses Hydra and writes tiles through omni::fabric::StageReaderWriter; no open specification or headers available.
- **`nucleus-omni-client-runtime`** (Unreachable)
  Closed NVIDIA runtime pieces. All Nucleus and omni.client responsibility stays on a separately authorized Kit
  extension; this repository ships no Nucleus or omni.client code.
- **`kit-extension-companion-repo`** (Excluded)
  The companion is specification-only in this repository. Implementation requires a separately authorized repository
  using current Kit extension mechanisms, not this codebase.
- **`physx-schema-vendoring`** (Excluded)
  PhysxSchema is never vendored into shipped packages. Externally supplied physx opinions are read and preserved as
  optional input only; project-owned openUsdPhysics covers advanced simulation domains.

## Kit execution evidence

Status: **pending**

Round-trip execution of OpenUsd-authored assets against a pinned headless Kit build, reopening Kit-authored outputs in
OpenUsd, and running the implemented openusd.bridge.v1 client against a live Kit session. The client protocol, its
bounds, its negotiation, and its reconnect/full-resync behaviour are implemented and locally proven against the
contract, an in-memory peer, and a Python protobuf/gRPC runtime; only execution against a real Kit or Nucleus process is
pending.

An authorized external job against a named Kit/Nucleus baseline. No such job exists in this repository yet. RTX
screenshots, if ever captured, are evidence of usability only and are never treated as raster-parity or execution
evidence.
